title: Expose the IBKR gateway's own login page URL via GET /api/ibkr/status
description:
User-requested feature (verbatim, split across two tasks): 'If ibkr is enabled, start check if user is authenticated. If not enable login button. When pressed on button, modal or browser window must open for initiating login.' The 'check if authenticated' half already exists end to end: `GET /api/ibkr/status` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py) already reports a `not_authenticated` state distinctly from `disabled`/`available`/`gateway_unreachable` (see `IBKRStatusResponse.state`'s own field description in backend/app/api/schemas.py), and the frontend already polls it every 30s (`useIbkrStatus`, `IbkrStatusIndicator` in the app bar) and displays a passive 'IBKR: Sign-in needed' badge (`components/common/IbkrStatusBadge`) for exactly that state. Nothing in this task changes that check.

What's missing, and what this task adds: the frontend has no way to know WHERE to actually send the user to log in. IBKR's Client Portal Gateway requires a one-time interactive browser login this app cannot automate (see `IBKRProvider`'s own module docstring) -- the gateway itself serves its own login page at its own base origin (e.g. `https://ibkr.home.arpa/` in this dev container's configuration, or `https://localhost:5000/` in IBKR's own documented default), which is a DIFFERENT URL from `Settings.ibkr_base_url` (`https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api`, the REST API root the app's own HTTP calls use) -- it's the same host/port but without the `/v1/api` API-root suffix, and is meant to be opened as a real page in a browser (interactive HTML form + IBKR's own 2FA flow), not called as a JSON API. This is backend-only knowledge today (`Settings.ibkr_base_url`) that the frontend has no way to derive correctly itself (hardcoding the `/v1/api` strip client-side would be fragile and duplicate backend config knowledge in the frontend).

This is the backend half: add a login-page URL to `GET /api/ibkr/status`'s response so the frontend has something safe and correct to open. The frontend half (`frontend-ibkr-login-button`, depends on this task) adds the actual button/window-opening UI.

checklist.step: Add a new field to `IBKRStatusResponse` (e.g. `login_url: str | None`) in `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, with a full `description` per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard explaining what it is (the gateway's own interactive login page, not the REST API root) and when it's populated.

In `get_ibkr_status` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py), derive the login URL from `Settings.ibkr_base_url`'s own origin (strip the `/v1/api` API-root suffix -- research and confirm this is genuinely IBKR's documented convention, don't just guess the string manipulation; record what you implemented against as a `decisions` entry, the same way `resolve_conid`'s own decisions entry documents the shape it was implemented against). Decide (and record as a `decisions` entry) which `state` value(s) this field should actually be populated for -- almost certainly `not_authenticated` (there's something to log into) and probably `available` too (so a user can still reach the login page manually, e.g. to re-auth a session about to expire), but NOT `disabled` (no gateway is even configured) or `gateway_unreachable` (the derived URL wouldn't be reachable either, since no gateway process answered at all).

Full CLAUDE.md API documentation standard compliance for the changed route/schema (docstring/summary already exist on the route -- update if this changes its meaning; new field gets a `description`). Regenerate `backend/openapi.json` via `python scripts/export_openapi.py` and confirm `frontend/src/api/types.ts` stays in sync.

Tests (mocked settings/config, no live network calls per docs/architecture/Testing.md): confirm `login_url` is populated correctly for the state(s) decided above and `None` for the others, and that the URL derivation is correct for at least one non-trivial `ibkr_base_url` value (e.g. one with a non-default port, one with a path prefix if IBKR's docs suggest that's ever valid). 90%+ coverage per the project-wide gate.

decisions.decision: The `/v1/api` REST-API-root suffix is genuinely IBKR's own documented gateway/API split, confirmed two independent ways rather than assumed: (1) empirically curling this dev container's real reachable gateway configured via `FINTRADE_IBKR_BASE_URL=https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api` (`FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED` stayed `false` throughout -- this was a manual sanity check, not something any automated test depends on): `GET https://ibkr.home.arpa/` (the origin with `/v1/api` stripped) returns a 302 redirect to `https://ibkr.home.arpa/sso/Login?forwardTo=22&RL=1&ip2loc=US` (the actual HTML login form), while `GET https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api/` returns a 404 'Resource not found' (confirming that path is REST-API-only, not a page). (2) Cross-checked against Voyz/ibeam (github.com/Voyz/ibeam, a widely used third-party IBKR gateway auto-login tool), whose `ibeam/src/var.py` defines `GATEWAY_BASE_URL = "https://localhost:5000"` (no `/v1/api`) as the base for BOTH `ROUTE_AUTH = '/sso/Login?forwardTo=22&RL=1&ip2loc=on'` (the interactive login route -- matching this dev container's own observed redirect target almost verbatim) AND every `/v1/api/...`-prefixed REST route (`ROUTE_AUTH_STATUS`, `ROUTE_TICKLE`, `ROUTE_LOGOUT`, etc.). Implemented `_ibkr_login_page_url` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py) to derive just the bare origin (with any leading path prefix preserved, minus the trailing `/v1/api`) rather than the full `/sso/Login?...` path with its query string, matching this task's own `description`'s example (`https://ibkr.home.arpa/` / `https://localhost:5000/`) -- the origin itself already redirects to the login form (observed above), so hardcoding IBKR's own internal `/sso/Login` route/query-param names into this app would be needless extra coupling to an implementation detail IBKR could change without notice.
decisions.rationale: resolve_conid's own decisions entry (docs/tasks/done/backend-ibkr-symbol-resolution.json) sets the precedent of recording exactly what a piece of IBKR-gateway-shape logic was implemented against, since this module's whole testing constraint (app/data/ibkr_provider.py's docstring) is that no sandboxed/CI environment has a live authenticated gateway to verify against -- here a live (if not fully authenticated) gateway WAS reachable via this dev container's own `.env` `FINTRADE_IBKR_BASE_URL`, so unlike most of this module's prior work this convention is empirically confirmed against a real gateway, not only against documentation/third-party tooling, and that's worth recording since it's a stronger evidence bar than usual for this codebase.

decisions.decision: `login_url` is populated (via `_LOGIN_URL_STATES` in backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py) for exactly `not_authenticated` and `available`, and left `null` for `disabled` and `gateway_unreachable` -- matching this checklist item's own suggested reasoning verbatim, verified rather than taken on faith: `disabled` means `Settings.ibkr_enabled` is `False` and `get_ibkr_provider` never even yields a provider, so there's no gateway configuration to derive a URL from in any meaningful sense; `gateway_unreachable` means `GET /iserver/auth/status` itself failed to get a response from any gateway process at the configured base URL, so a browser opening the derived origin would almost certainly hit the same unreachable host/port and fail identically (confirmed against this dev container's own reachable gateway: the derivation only found a working login redirect because a process WAS actually listening -- if nothing were listening, the browser navigation would simply fail, same as the `/iserver/auth/status` request did). `available` was kept in (not excluded) because a session nearing expiry is a real, user-facing scenario this app has no way to distinguish from a freshly-authenticated one via `state` alone -- offering a manual re-auth link costs nothing when the gateway is already reachable.
decisions.rationale: No alternative seriously considered beyond the checklist's own suggestion (also populating for `gateway_unreachable` on the theory that 'the user might fix the gateway and then want to click login' was briefly considered but rejected: that URL would be a guess about a host/port that has already been shown not to answer requests right now, which is a worse failure mode --a link that silently fails when clicked -- than omitting it and relying on the existing `detail` text to explain the gateway isn't running).

review.notes: Full review of PR #342. Independently re-derived the `/v1/api`-suffix convention rather than trusting the task-worker's report: curled this dev container's own reachable IBKR gateway myself -- `GET https://ibkr.home.arpa/` -> 302 redirect to `.../sso/Login?forwardTo=22&RL=1&ip2loc=US`, `GET https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api/` -> 404 -- both match the task-worker's claimed results exactly. Read `_ibkr_login_page_url` directly and exercised it with my own arbitrary inputs beyond the test file's own cases (custom host/port/path-prefix combos, a query-string URL, a URL not ending in `/v1/api`) -- matches documented/tested behavior in every case. Read `get_ibkr_status` in full: `login_url` populated only for `not_authenticated`/`available`, `None` for `disabled`/`gateway_unreachable`; reasoning is sound, and the new `settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)` parameter changes no other route behavior. Confirmed the rewritten `test_ibkr_status.py` no longer depends on this container's real `.env`: ran the full file both with `.env` present and with it renamed away -- identical 11/11 pass either way; also drove the endpoint directly with my own arbitrary `FINTRADE_IBKR_BASE_URL` override not present in the test file and got the correctly-derived `login_url` back. API documentation standard: `login_url` has a full `description`, route docstring updated; regenerated `backend/openapi.json` myself via `python scripts/export_openapi.py` -- byte-identical to what's committed; diffed `frontend/src/api/types.ts` against the pre-PR commit and confirmed the new field/description match `schemas.py` verbatim. Static analysis: backend `ruff check .` and `mypy` clean; frontend `yarn lint` and `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` clean; `scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py` clean; `scripts/validate_tasks.py` clean (330 files). Full backend suite: 1450 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`tests/unit/test_config.py::test_ibkr_base_url_defaults_to_localhost_gateway`) -- confirmed this is the same long-documented, unrelated `.env`-override issue tracked across multiple prior PRs (e.g. `backend-ibkr-portfolio-preload-followups*`), not introduced by this PR (its diff touches zero lines of `test_config.py`); 100% coverage on the changed files, well above the 90% gate. Both checklist items phrased as 'decide X' have corresponding `decisions` entries with real rationale -- no undocumented judgment call. Area is `backend/api`, not `backend/signals`/`backend/portfolio`, so verify-elder-signal doesn't apply; no new module/dependency/layer, so architecture-review doesn't apply; no frontend component touched (no current frontend consumer of the new field -- that's the dependent `frontend-ibkr-login-button` task), so no component-placement review applies. No UI-facing surface in this PR (backend-only, additive optional field with no frontend consumer yet) -- browser walkthrough (step 9) and the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) explicitly skipped rather than silently omitted. Ran the code-review skill (effort: high) independently against the diff -- zero findings, corroborating the above. No blocking or non-blocking findings; no follow-up task filed.
